instructions: See docs/ratings.md. Give every season a rating on the absolute scale. Rate the player that season, never their career.

seasons.note: Eighteen, technically advanced and already comfortable in possession at the top level; the good WBA midfielder was clearly visible.
A combative but technically sound midfielder who went on to a French title and a Roma career; one of Everton’s better players that season.
His best English season: a first-choice midfielder in a Champions League semi-final side and the one who made it function defensively.
Converted from a raw centre-half into Arsenal’s holding midfielder, and by this season the best player at the club in that position.
A regular in the Villa midfield at 19 and already a neat, intelligent passer; slight, and easily bullied out of games.
A poor year in a relegated Fulham side; the passing was still there but he was overrun physically week to week.
The best pure ball-winner in the league that season, which is what a mid-season move to Tottenham for twelve million pounds was paying for.
Squeezed out at Tottenham and no longer the ball-winner Wigan sold; the drop is real, not rotation.
Played most of this season in central midfield rather than at centre-back; a fine athlete and reader of the game, not yet the defender he became.
Moved to centre-back in the second half of the season and looked immediately at home; the jump is the position, not a sudden gain in ability.
An ever-present centre-half in the PFA team of the year: the season he became the best defender in the division rather than a fine athlete playing there.
Rated on ability rather than starts: a rotation forward at Chelsea by squad depth, not standard — technically excellent and a Norway regular.
Five starts before the November move to Rangers; the rating covers the player, not the minutes.
Genuinely quick and a natural finisher, but a non-league signing eighteen months earlier; the ability was raw.
Seven starts; a broken leg and then a stress fracture cost him most of two seasons.
Three starts in two years; the leg break and then the stress fracture had taken the pace that was most of his game.
Twelve goals in Wigan’s first top-flight season and about the quickest forward in the division that year.
A 52-cap Germany international, but at 30 in his final season and physically finished; rated well below his Stuttgart peak.
Liverpool’s player of the season in a bad year for the club; the reading of the game and the ball retention had both caught up with the effort.
A visibly erratic season - the Deportivo and Arsenal errors were not one-offs - from a keeper who had been the best in the league a year earlier.
